name: nov-2-8
note: First batch under the reboot (RULES.md, The voice; F-007 to F-009). Planned Oct 30 from the footage that exists: none. The Drive inbox was empty in all five folders, so the week is the thin week the reboot doc names: the Wednesday comment-COOKBOOK post, the Thursday send-this (st03, series ledger, already scheduled) and one pin a day at 12:10 PT from the unused stock photos (the last week stock is allowed: F-008 cuts it off Nov 15). Every photo opened before use; descriptions in photos.json. Shell from the post's job: bleed where the food fills the frame and the type needs a scrim, the paper photo shell where the picture is an object on a flat colour and the headline wants clean paper. Captions are text messages: lowercase, the pain first, the dish and the number, what iEatz did in one line, no method (F-006). Pins link to the breakfasts page where the pin is a breakfast, else the App Store (no other page exists; ieatzhealthy.com is not reachable from this session so the page contents were not re-read). [2026-10-30 14:00 PT: seven of Travis's own photos landed in the Drive inbox the same afternoon; every frame except the receipt pin (no own receipt photo yet) was rebuilt on them as v2. Own phone photos render ungraded (grade false): nothing styled.]

posts.photoClaim: one avocado half with the stone, centred on a pink background
posts.head: The avocado is ripe today. Only today.
posts.why: The ripe window is a joke everyone who has bought an avocado has lived: a 24-hour countdown sitting on the counter. The fix is the eggs next to it.
posts.app: Tell iEatz what is on the counter (an avocado, eggs, bread) and it writes the breakfast with calories and protein estimated; anything missing goes to Instacart.
posts.note: 2026-10-30 14:00 PT: replaced by the v2 frame on one of Travis's own photos (Drive inbox, Oct 29); the stock frame never scheduled

posts.photoClaim: cucumber slices, kale, spinach, lime, celery and herbs arranged in a grid on a mint green background
posts.head: Wilting greens are three dinners, not trash.
posts.sub: Kale, spinach, cucumber, a lime. Tell iEatz what is going soft and it writes tonight from exactly that, protein counted.
posts.why: The surprise is the reframe: the sad drawer reads as a loss and is three dinners nobody has picked yet. Everyone has thrown out this exact bag.
posts.app: Add what is going soft to iEatz and it writes the recipe from those items with calories and protein estimated; missing items to Instacart.
posts.note: 2026-10-30 14:00 PT: replaced by the v2 frame on one of Travis's own photos (Drive inbox, Oct 29); the stock frame never scheduled

posts.photoClaim: a shopper in a brown coat walking away down a supermarket aisle with a blue basket, wine shelves on the left and empty shelves on the right
posts.head: One receipt. Five dinners. Zero planning.
posts.sub: Shop on vibes. Snap the receipt at the register and iEatz writes the week from what is actually in the basket, protein counted.
posts.why: The promise with numbers: the thing you already walk out with (a receipt) is the meal plan you never make. The shopper with no list is every one of us on a Wednesday.
posts.app: Receipt import: snap the receipt and iEatz writes the week's dinners from the items on it, calories and protein estimated, the missing items handed to Instacart.

posts.photoClaim: a tall beef burger with lettuce, tomato and onion on a seeded bun, a pick through the top, on a slate with potato wedges, a red leather booth behind
posts.head: 30 dinners you'd actually eat. Comment COOKBOOK.
posts.why: The weekly ask with the offer as the whole frame. A free cookbook has one thing to prove to a stranger: that the food is food you want. The burger says it before the headline does, so it sits in the light, not under a scrim.
posts.app: The cookbook: 30 recipes, each with a tap-to-shop Instacart list, delivered by DM when someone comments COOKBOOK.
posts.note: 2026-10-30 14:00 PT: replaced by the v2 frame on one of Travis's own photos (Drive inbox, Oct 29); the stock frame never scheduled

posts.photoClaim: a breakfast plate close up: halved hard boiled eggs, cherry tomatoes, mozzarella balls, grilled sausage and toast on a dark wooden table
posts.head: Eggs, tomatoes, toast. Breakfast in 10.
posts.sub: Tell iEatz the three and it writes it. About 22 g protein, estimated.
posts.why: Three things most fridges hold, a time and a protein number: the promise is that breakfast is already decided, you just have to say the words.
posts.app: Add the three to iEatz and it writes the breakfast with calories and protein estimated.
posts.note: 2026-10-30 14:00 PT: replaced by the v2 frame on one of Travis's own photos (Drive inbox, Oct 29); the stock frame never scheduled

posts.photoClaim: a cafe plate on a yellow dish: avocado toast topped with a soft egg and pickled onion, a pile of scrambled eggs, beet slaw and greens, on a mosaic table
posts.head: Brunch line: 40 minutes. Your kitchen: 10.
posts.sub: An avocado, two eggs, bread. Tell iEatz what is there and it writes this plate, protein counted.
posts.why: The number everyone standing outside a brunch place has done in their head. The plate in the photo is the plate you waited for, made from three things you own.
posts.app: Tell iEatz what is in the kitchen (avocado, eggs, bread) and it writes the plate with calories and protein estimated; out of bread, it goes to Instacart.
posts.note: 2026-10-30 14:00 PT: replaced by the v2 frame on one of Travis's own photos (Drive inbox, Oct 29); the stock frame never scheduled

posts.photoClaim: ground spices and seeds in antique spoons laid out on white marble with chillies, bay leaves and lemongrass
posts.head: Bland chicken again? Your spice drawer disagrees.
posts.why: The same chicken three nights running is the real weeknight problem; the fix was in the drawer the whole time. The spoons show the ingredient nobody counts as one.
posts.app: Tell iEatz the chicken and the three jars you can reach and it writes a new dinner with calories and protein estimated; the missing item goes to Instacart.
posts.note: 2026-10-30 14:00 PT: replaced by the v2 frame on one of Travis's own photos (Drive inbox, Oct 29); the stock frame never scheduled

posts.photoClaim: a bowl of berries, rhubarb stalks, blood orange and grapefruit halves along the left edge of a white surface, the rest of the frame empty
posts.head: Bought Sunday. Trash by Thursday. Not this week.
posts.sub: Berries, rhubarb, citrus. Tell iEatz what is in the bowl and it writes the breakfasts that use it up before anything turns.
posts.why: The Sunday fruit haul that dies by Thursday is a weekly ritual of guilt; the post names the cycle and ends it in three words.
posts.app: Tell iEatz what is in the fruit bowl and it writes the breakfasts and snacks from it, calories and protein estimated; the yogurt you are out of goes to Instacart.
posts.note: 2026-10-30 14:00 PT: replaced by the v2 frame on one of Travis's own photos (Drive inbox, Oct 29); the stock frame never scheduled

posts.photoClaim: a bunless burger bowl on a wooden table: a beef patty under lettuce, tomato, avocado and a pickle in a white bowl, a bowl of fries and a stacked burger behind it
posts.head: Forgot the buns. Didn't go back.
posts.why: The brand in one frame: a real burger night in a real kitchen, no bun, no store run, still dinner. The surprise is that it got better, not worse.
posts.app: Add the four ingredients to iEatz and it writes the burger bowl with calories and protein estimated; the bun goes to Instacart if you want it.
chips: buns to Instacart, if you must

posts.photoClaim: a stove from above: a pan of red coconut curry with peppers and a wooden spoon, a tray of browned tofu cubes, a bowl of cooked grain, a cast iron pan on the back burner
posts.head: One can of coconut milk. Dinner, decided.
posts.why: The stove mid-mess is the proof: this is a Tuesday, not a shoot. The promise is one pantry can turning the leftovers into a real dinner.
posts.app: Add what is in the fridge and the can to iEatz and it writes the curry with calories and protein estimated; missing items to Instacart.

posts.photoClaim: sheet-pan nachos on a baking tray: tortilla chips under melted cheese, mushrooms, cherry tomatoes, jalapeno slices and dollops of guacamole, a bowl of guacamole beside it
posts.head: 30 dinners you'd actually eat. Comment COOKBOOK.
posts.why: The weekly ask with the offer as the whole frame, on our own food for the first time: a tray of nachos from a real kitchen says "you would eat this" better than any stock plate did.
posts.app: The cookbook: 30 recipes, each with a tap-to-shop Instacart list, delivered by DM when someone comments COOKBOOK.

posts.photoClaim: a stack of five pancakes on a white plate on a wooden table, a bottle of maple syrup behind it, flowers and a living room out of focus
posts.head: No pancake mix in the house. Pancakes anyway.
posts.why: The box is the thing people think they need; the stack says the pantry had it the whole time. Weekend breakfast is the most-saved pin category we post into.
posts.app: Tell iEatz flour, eggs and milk and it writes the pancakes with calories and protein estimated; out of syrup, it goes to Instacart.

posts.photoClaim: a set table from above: a cutting board with sliced steak, a bowl of ravioli with herbs and parmesan, a bowl of broccoli, candles, pink napkins, a hand reaching in at the top
posts.head: Date night at home. 25 minutes.
posts.sub: A steak, a bag of ravioli, a head of broccoli. Tell iEatz the three and it writes the whole table, protein counted.
posts.why: A hand, candles, a real table: the first frame with a person in it. The promise is the restaurant night for the price of three things already in the fridge.
posts.app: Add the three to iEatz and it writes the steak, the ravioli and the side with calories and protein estimated; missing items to Instacart.

posts.photoClaim: a sheet pan of roasted purple sweet potato chunks and slabs of squash, some charred, on a wooden table
posts.head: Half a squash, two potatoes. One tray.
posts.sub: The half squash and the sweet potatoes rolling around the drawer. Tell iEatz and it writes the tray, protein counted.
posts.why: The sad half squash everyone has in the drawer, shown as what it becomes: one tray, charred edges, a real kitchen. The number is one, and that is the point.
posts.app: Add the squash and the potatoes to iEatz and it writes the sheet-pan dinner with calories and protein estimated; the missing protein goes to Instacart.

posts.photoClaim: a holiday plate on an orange plaid runner: sliced turkey, mashed potatoes, salad greens and stuffing, mini pumpkins and a paper towel roll behind it
posts.head: One roast. Three more dinners hiding in it.
posts.why: The Sunday plate everyone photographs, reframed as Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. The paper towel roll stays in frame: nothing styled.
posts.app: Add the leftovers to iEatz and it writes the next dinners from them with calories and protein estimated; the missing items go to Instacart.
